question: Should OpenClaw adopt a new process-wide localization foundation that localizes existing human CLI output from OPENCLAW_LOCALE and platform locale variables before the remaining four cumulative bundles are reviewed?
rationale: This PR creates a new cross-package runtime and changes presentation behavior across existing operator surfaces; the correct default, supported locales, and compatibility promise are product and ownership decisions rather than a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Sponsor the staged foundation
options.body: Approve the shared runtime direction, require the bounded changelog and proof repairs, then review the remaining bundles against this agreed contract.

options.title: Narrow the first boundary
options.body: Keep only the registry and existing UI/onboarding convergence here, deferring CLI and gateway presentation adoption until their compatibility contract is separately approved.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Do not introduce the shared localization package until a maintainer-owned RFC decision defines the supported product scope and upgrade expectations.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the shared runtime direction, require the bounded changelog and proof repairs, then review the remaining bundles against this agreed contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contact across the preceding and current localization-series proposals; a repository owner should ultimately sponsor the product decision.
